_what: Copy to .claude/turn-checks.json to add checks to the end-of-turn hook (.claude/hooks/turn-check.mjs) or disable a default one. Each check fires on the turn's final answer only, and blocks once.
_requires: search = a search ran this turn · look = a search ran or a file was read whole · any-call = any tool ran · compute = a call computed something (node -e, python, awk, bc, jq, a project script) · run-after-edit = something ran after the turn's last edit, searches and rereads aside · last-call-ok = the last call did not error · cite = the sentence itself carries the `cite` pattern (a reference, an attribution, or a reservation). The defaults and what each requires: node .claude/hooks/turn-check.mjs --list
_language: Opt-in: "fr" or "en". Blocks a turn whose text, the short narration between tool calls included, holds a sentence in the other language. Code, paths, commands, URLs, quotations, blockquotes and table rows are not read. Brought by a register that logged six English transition sentences in one night under a written rule to answer in French. To turn it on, add "language": "fr" to your copy.
_commitTrailers: Opt-in: "forbid" holds any git commit carrying a Co-Authored-By trailer for a person's yes (.claude/hooks/send-guard.mjs); a list of keys holds those instead, e.g. ["Co-Authored-By", "Signed-off-by"]. Brought by an owner who forbade tool co-signatures in her repos, after one went in four times. To turn it on, add "commitTrailers": "forbid" to your copy.
_sharedIndex: On by default: the send guard (.claude/hooks/send-guard.mjs) asks before git add -A, --all or ., git commit -a, and git stash, which sweep the index every session in a clone shares. A project where one session works at a time turns it off with "sharedIndex": false.

checks._why: A rule of law stated from memory, with an exact-sounding reason, closes the question for the owner: the one case where a wrong answer is believed precisely because it is argued. Brought by a workshop whose agent justified an omission with a rule it had not read, twice in an hour. Cite, attribute, or say you do not know; never deduce.
patterns: \b(l'administration|le fisc|la loi|le code|la jurisprudence|la doctrine)\b[^.]{0,80}\b(retient|impose|exige|interdit|permet|exonère|s'applique|ne s'applique pas)\b
checks.cite: \b(article|art\.|BOI-|BOFiP|légifrance|legifrance|arrêt|décision|cass\.|CE,|selon|d'après|according to|section|§|lu le|read on|à vérifier|sous réserve|je ne sais pas|to be confirmed|I do not know)\b
checks.say: states a rule of law with no reference, no attribution and no reservation in the same sentence. Cite the text and the date you read it, say who says it, or say it is to be checked with the adviser. Withdrawing such a statement needs the same evidence as making it.
